title: Batch rigorous cubic relation logs
objective: Replace per-relation Arb log resource calls in the complex cubic dependency pipeline with one rigorous batched call while preserving exact output intervals and fallback semantics

handoff.summary: Factors unique-real-root isolation out of scalar cubic log enclosure, exposes exact absolute embedding numerator intervals, and replaces two Arb resource calls per retained relation with one positive-rational-log batch for all 2*n interval endpoints. The batch and serial paths produce bit-for-bit identical rigorous endpoints natively and with native execution disabled. The full cubic receipt, exact replay, pinned LMFDB, and large-unit suite passes. A direct FLINT resource microbenchmark at 36 relations measured 128.8 us for 72 singleton calls versus 20.5 us for one batch (about 6.3x for this resource phase).
risks: The integration branch independently refactored the same root-isolation helpers, so cherry-pick may conflict around _cubic_real_log_bounds; preserve the integration branch's root helper and merge the absolute-bounds/batch helper plus dependency-phase allocation and call semantically.

pnpm architecture:check passed FFI, package, native, Wasm capability/resource, and CoWasm checks, then failed because the branch base has a stale generated optimizer-opportunity manifest outside this lane's claims.

pnpm test:native passed all functional, native-kernel, sanitizer, lifecycle, and migration suites, then failed the unrelated dense QQ performance gate: select_rows_300, select_columns_300, and stack_300x300 take about 35 ms on this branch base against 15 ms budgets. A standalone rerun reproduced only those same performance failures.
The microbenchmark isolates the Arb resource-call phase; the full wider-corpus wall-time effect must be measured after integration with the f+14/f+18 relation prefix.
next_steps: Integrate the batch helper into the current wider-prefix cubic campaign and measure dependency-phase and 1000-field corpus wall time on opt.
Use the exposed absolute embedding intervals as the rigorous input boundary for the transformed approximate-log sidecar.
